method: Independent standard-library raw JSON checks, SHA256 payload checks and direct paired log-ratio Student-t calculation; no project analyzer imports or GPU execution.
limitations: Native expected output bytes are retained only in process: their reported hashes are consistent across processes and protected by reviewed byte-comparison code; the native hash cannot be recomputed from the saved reports alone.
CPU fixture hashes and 40 selected original tensor hashes were recomputed, but CPU matrix multiplication was not rerun in this review.

Wall is the sum of coordinator windows and excludes cache invalidation/priming; device counters cover the whole arm including preparation and other processes. Matching byte counts establish exercised device reads, not per-process attribution or cold NAND.
Shared trace and timing use separate processes; trace occupancy describes the captured 64 executions per arm, not timing or normal requests.
GPU intervals include shared and routed work; they cannot be split into exclusive kernel costs.
Control and shared conditions are separate processes, not paired measurements of shared-work cost.
Eight experts span four layers; no routing, full attention/recurrent work, final MoE reduction or full-token scratch lifetime is represented.
Nominal thermal/power and boundary memory observations do not rule out brief unobserved changes. Existing system swap is nonzero; only lack of growth is checked.

Five within-process paired observations use marginal Student-t log-ratio intervals and may have temporal correlation. They do not qualify normal-request speed, 5 tokens/s, quality or production selection.
recommendation: The packed advantage survives both the unchanged mixed-arrival control and added actual shared prelude. Keep the rejected production selection unchanged. A separately declared full-token scratch lifetime replay is the next narrow missing condition, not an established explanation or justification for an I/O-scheduler change.
